argument: Many physiological rates, lifespans, structures, and ecological quantities scale approximately as powers of body mass, $Y=Y_0M^b$. Such relations reveal geometric, transport, energetic, and life-history constraints across size ranges.
boundary: Exponents vary among taxa, traits, temperature regimes, and statistical methods.
A fitted power law need not imply one universal network mechanism.
Phylogenetic nonindependence and restricted ranges can bias slopes.
claim: Many physiological rates, lifespans, structures, and ecological quantities scale approximately as powers of body mass, $Y=Y_0M^b$. Such relations reveal geometric, transport, energetic, and life-history constraints across size ranges.
interpretation: Principia should preserve taxonomic range and uncertainty in exponent $b$. “Three-quarter law” is not exact across all organisms and conditions.

migration_provenance.source_basics: Kleiber documented metabolic scaling in the 1930s. West, Brown, and Enquist proposed network-based quarter-power explanations in the 1990s, sparking extensive debate.

review_attestation.basis: Explicit owner bulk attestation for the repaired Meta-Principles v2 corpus.

scope.basics: Kleiber documented metabolic scaling in the 1930s. West, Brown, and Enquist proposed network-based quarter-power explanations in the 1990s, sparking extensive debate.

questions: What unit, environment, timescale, and heritable variation make the new biological Principle operate?
Does the claim separate selection, drift, constraint, plasticity, and feedback?

title: Biological Rates and Forms Scale Systematically with Size
